messages.subject: Question about % variance explained
parts:
Dear Karl,

I apologize that this question is pretty similar to some other questions. When estimating the effects of the QTL with fitqtl, I get a % variance explained by the model and % variance of each QTL (the drop one analysis). The % variance explained by the model is always higher (sometimes quite substantially) than the % variances of the individual QTL/covariates. 

I see a few people saying that the % variance of the model is lower than the sum of the individual variances due to correlated genotypes/covariates. But I'm not sure why the model would be able to explain more variance than the individual components. Do you have any insight about why this is? 

Thank you very much,
Andrew

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Question about % variance explained
parts:
The overall percent variance explained will only equal the sum of the individual QTLs' percent variance explained if the genotypes at the QTLs are perfectly independent. Whether the overall percent variance explained is > or < the sum of the individual QTLs' PVE depends on the positive or negative association between QTL genotypes.

karl
